text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

The two pairs of eyes held each other through an entire exhale.
And then the young man had pushed himself up on the armrests, stretched to his full height, and strolled over to shake her hand.
“Mara?”
He was closer than she would have guessed from where he’d been sitting, broad-shouldered and strong-chinned in a white T-shirt, grinning at her through dark-framed glasses as he reached out for the handshake. She took it.
“Jonah,” he said.
“Hello,” she replied, and then they stood there, still shaking hands, not knowing what to do next.

And that was when a door opened down the hallway behind her, releasing two voices into the room. One female, one male; one asking a question, the other replying; neither loud nor excited, just casual conversation. Jonah released her hand and turned away to look down the hall at them.
When Mara heard the voices and followed his gaze, she saw one young man who wasn’t Jonah, but close in size and shape; he had brown hair and a beard and was carrying a glass.

The brown-haired man glanced once over his shoulder, saw them standing there, nodded hello, and stepped right into the gathering, holding up his glass of wine—a half-full plastic cup with the Fulcrum logo on it. “Cheers.” He set it on the table against the wall to the left of the door, and stepped forward to shake Jonah’s hand as they exchanged names.

As he set down the glass and moved out of its space, a previously unseen catering worker entered from the hallway behind him and retrieved it. She wore the same black-and-white striped Fulcrum uniform shirt, though she looked old enough to have had that job since the Institute was founded; and she gave no outward sign of the social fact that she was taking their discarded drink back to the kitchen, while the rest of the conversation went on.

Mara watched this woman return to the hallway where she belonged, and noticed herself noticing who assumed whose labor.

segment:
The third man from the hallway followed the other two into the common room, a long-haired, big-boned individual in a deep voice that said “Good evening” and “Adrian.” He didn’t make for either Mara or Jonah but instead paused by the table beside the door where he picked up a plastic glass of wine, walked out into the middle of the floor, and held his hand up in a toast. “Cheers, everyone.”

The other two raised hands with cups or glasses, Jonah making do with his glass of water, and they clinked together briefly, before taking turns sitting on the long couch. Jonah invited Mara to join him there and she sat down at the end opposite him; when Adrian started speaking, he directed his attention mostly at her. “Good to meet you, Mara. What can I tell you?”

Mara blinked, taken aback. It was a little early to jump straight into questions. “Er, you’re one of the Fulcrum directors?”
Adrian nodded, sitting on the floor at Mara’s feet and looking up at her from between the couch cushions. “Yes. What else do you want to know?”

“Well,” she started, still mildly shocked but turning it toward the next idea. “What’s the purpose of tonight’s party?”

“That,” said Adrian, his eyes twinkling with some inner amusement, “is a very good question. And we haven’t actually talked about it yet, so why don’t we? Jonah—have you and Mara discussed that question?”

Jonah gave a slight shake of his head, watching the exchange closely from where he lay sprawled at the other end of the couch, eyes narrowed behind those heavy frames of his.

segment:
They were interrupted by the sound of another door opening, and Adrian stepping into the room with a fresh cup in one hand and a pile of papers in the other.
Mara tensed before she consciously knew why, but when Adrian greeted Jonah with a smile and set down both the papers and the glass on the low table, he made eye contact with Mara again. He looked at her intently, and she couldn’t tell whether she was under scrutiny or not. But he was looking at her.
“Good evening. Mara, right? I’m Adrian.”
She shook hands, too, and then everyone glanced down at the new cup of wine on the table. Adrian glanced from that back up to them, and seemed to realize something. He tapped the side of his own head, as if to say, Whoops, forget that for now. “Don’t worry about the drinks,” he told Mara. “The catering crew’s still here until seven.”
Mara wasn’t quite sure what he meant. She wondered if Adrian’s wife was the one who’d set up tonight’s audition process.
